title: haven: mimi-hubd requires a client certificate in the TLS handshake at 34eae7e, so a peer gets no HTTP answer
description:
Verified 2026-11-22 against our own copy of mimi-hubd at 34eae7e, run by
tools/interop/haven/live/run.sh. Mark authorized running our own Haven
instances, which is what made this checkable without touching Jason's
hub.

OBSERVED, and ruled out as our bug first (bead mimid-7yn7.9):

  POST https://localhost:8443/mimi/pl/update/x, From: mimi@b.example
    without a client certificate -> curl code 000, TLS handshake fails
    with the harness client certificate -> 404, i.e. TLS completed and
      the request was routed (404 only because the path was invented)

So the handshake itself is refused when no client certificate is
presented. The pair is what makes it conclusive: the same URL, the same
CA, differing only by the client certificate.

Ruled out on our side before concluding:
- hostname mismatch. mimi-hubd's server certificate is CN=localhost with
  SAN DNS:localhost, IP:127.0.0.1, and the selftest connects to
  localhost:8443, so the name matches. (A diagnostic of mine used
  haven.localhost:8443, which did NOT match and produced the same 000
  for an unrelated reason; certs.sh now also names haven.localhost so
  that confusion does not recur.)
- CA trust. openssl s_client reports "Verify return code: 0 (ok)".
- a wrong client certificate path. An earlier run of mine used
  client.crt/client.key, which do not exist; the files are
  client.pem/client-key.pem.

WHY IT MATTERS. Our own selftest comment recorded that at d750a8d
mimi-hubd completed TLS without a client certificate and refused at the
HTTP layer with 403, because a request could carry a signature instead.
At 34eae7e it does not. Both are defensible, and handshake enforcement
is arguably MORE conformant to protocol-07 §4.1's "MUST be mutually
authenticated" -- but the consequence for a peer is different:

A handshake refusal carries no reason. A peer whose certificate is
missing, expired or issued by the wrong CA learns only that TLS failed.
Compare mimid, which since mimid-75nk.12 answers 403 with a `reason`
member naming the peer's own DNS record, signature or certificate. On an
interop day, "TLS failed" against a peer with no obligation to help
costs hours.

ALSO WORTH KNOWING: it means mimid cannot talk to a hub in this mode at
all without [peer_tls.identity] configured, since there is no
signature-only fallback. That is exactly the half still blocked on Jason
(mimid-1wgh.46.20.1 item 4), so it moves from optional to required if
Jason's hub behaves as our copy does. Check his before the interop day;
asking him needs Mark's OK.

selftest.sh now accepts either shape and says which, rather than
asserting the one Haven happened to do at d750a8d.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-11-22, same day: the escalation this bead implied does
NOT apply to Jason's deployed hub. Checked it directly:

  POST https://mimi.havenmessenger.com:8443/mimi/pl/identifierQuery/example.com
    no client certificate -> HTTP 403, so TLS COMPLETED
  openssl s_client -msg -> exactly 1 CertificateRequest

So the public hub asks for a client certificate but does not require
one, and refuses at the HTTP layer instead: the d750a8d behaviour this
bead's description says changed. Effectively "mode request", the same
shape as mimid's own Caddy configuration.

So either Jason runs a different commit than our copy at 34eae7e, or the
enforcement is configurable and his deployment does not turn it on. Both
behaviours exist in the wild and a peer cannot tell which it faces until
it tries.

CONSEQUENCE: [peer_tls.identity] is NOT required to reach Jason's hub
today, and mimid-1wgh.46.20.1's note saying otherwise is corrected.
mimid already talks to it successfully with signatures alone, proven by
the signed identifierQuery that returned 200.

The finding itself stands and is still worth telling him: our copy of
mimi-hubd at 34eae7e DOES refuse the handshake, so whatever he deploys
in January decides whether signature-only peers can reach him at all.
Worth asking which mode he intends for the interop day, since the answer
changes what every other implementation needs to bring. Asking needs
Mark's OK.

Also recorded: his server certificate is from Let's Encrypt, so it
chains to the public roots and mimid needs no [peer_tls] roots entry for
it.
